title: stream lexer: trailing-byte-reserve and ordered handoff to prevent partial-json and fncall reordering
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Fixes intermittent partial-JSON emissions in SSE caused by UTF-8 multi-byte split across chunks; improves determinism of function-call/event ordering during stream handoff; no API changes.
description: Motivation: Customers reported sporadic partial JSON objects arriving in the SSE stream when a multi-byte UTF-8 character is split across network chunks; additionally, high-concurrency tool/function call flows could produce out-of-order fncall boundaries in rare interleaving windows. This PR introduces a small stream-lexer component in the streaming path that reserves trailing bytes to avoid splitting UTF-8 codepoints at chunk boundaries and adds an ordered handoff gate for fncall/toolcall events to preserve logical ordering across internal buffering and backpressure events. This is intended to be a minimal, low-latency change that prevents user-facing partial JSON and tool/function call reordering without changing existing stream framing or client behavior. Changes made: 1) stream/lexer/byte_reserve.go: new lexer that inspects outgoing chunks and ensures the last up-to-4 bytes (configurable) are held until the next chunk arrives if they form an incomplete UTF-8 sequence; emits a safe boundary marker when the sequence completes to aid downstream parsers. 2) stream/handshake/ordered_handoff.go: introduces a small gate that sequences fncall/toolcall terminal events by assigning a monotonic stream-epoch and only allowing the epoch to advance once the previous epoch has observed its terminal sentinel (reduces rare races when KV cache flushes + rebuffering cause swapped call boundaries). 3) integrations/openai_compat/sse_adapter.go: wires lexer and handoff into the OpenAI compatibility adapter so hosted and compatible routing paths benefit. 4) unit and integration tests: new tests that fuzz-chunk UTF-8 splits, simulate backpressure pause/resume, and assert JSON recomposition and call ordering invariants. Checklist: - [x] Design doc sketched in ENG-1428 - [x] Unit tests for byte-reserve lexer - [x] Integration test for fncall ordered handoff - [x] Load smoke to validate latency impact < 2% p50 - [x] Backcompat: no changes to API surface - [x] Added metrics: stream.byte_reserve_events, stream.handoff_latency Summary of commits: - c1a2b3 introduce stream lexer and byte reservation algorithm - d4e5f6 add ordered handoff gate and epoch sequencing - f7a8b9 wire components into openai_compat adapter and add metrics - a1b2c3 add unit/integration fuzz tests and fixes - b2c3d4 tidy up logging and add feature flag (alpha) Files changed (high-level): - stream/lexer/byte_reserve.go: new - stream/lexer/byte_reserve_test.go: new - stream/handshake/ordered_handoff.go: new - stream/handshake/ordered_handoff_test.go: new - integrations/openai_compat/sse_adapter.go: modified (hooked lexer/handoff, added metrics) - integrations/openai_compat/sse_adapter_test.go: modified (updated test vectors) - metrics/registry.go: added two counters/gauges - docs/streaming.md: note about byte-reserve behavior and troubleshooting (small section) Review conversation: - Diego Ramirez (reviewer): "Overall this looks reasonable; only concern is the feature flag gating for the lexer — can we make it opt-in for now and enable by default in nightly? Also add benchmarks for p99." - Elena Park (author): "Added feature flag (alpha) and benchmark entry; default enabled in nightly runs only. Bench numbers included in the PR comments." - Asha Menon: "Ordered handoff looks correct but please add a comment describing why we choose monotonic epoch vs sequence number in the code - helps future debuggers." - Elena Park: "Added code comment and a short note in streaming.md explaining the epoch choice (avoids gaps when ephemeral replays occur)." - Samir Gupta: "Two test flakes observed in CI on first run (integration/timeouts) — I retriggered CI." CI checks: - unit: pass - integration: flaky on first run, passed on rerun - lint: pass - bench-nightly: recorded (p50 +1.4%, p99 +0.7%) Observed behavior and mitigation: - Partial JSON: prior to this change we observed ~1 in 50k streams encountering a truncated multi-byte sequence that would cause JSON decode errors on the client. With byte-reserve enabled in nightly, we saw zero reproductions in a 48-hour fuzz run. - Fncall reordering: repro requires a tight interleaving of toolcall terminal flush + rebuffer + resend; the ordered handoff prevents the epoch from advancing until the previous terminal is observed, eliminating the reordering window in integration fuzz. Performance: microbenchmarks show negligible p50 latency impact (+1.4%) and p99 increase under worst-case backpressure scenarios of ~0.7% which is acceptable for the hosted workload and can be toggled with the feature flag. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in nightly for 48 hours, run extended fuzz and canary in us-east-1 traffic at 5% for 72 hours, monitor stream.json_decode_errors, stream.byte_reserve_events, and stream.handoff_latency. If stable, promote to full rollout over 7 days. Merge details: merged by Diego Ramirez using squash on 2026-02-28 after approvals. Notes: this change is focused on stability and compatibility; it is intentionally conservative and guarded behind a feature flag to allow quick rollback if any anomaly is observed. Related: ENG-1428 design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1428/stream-lexer-byte-reserve. Logs and bench artifacts attached to the PR for auditors.
